question: RULE on DEC-3: May Cargento run git status inside a user working repository — a subprocess in their code, not a file read in a store — and publish, per session, only whether the tree is dirty and how many entries changed? Options A (no repository access at all), B (dirty/clean and a count), C (B plus branch and upstream state), D (C plus a remote call for PR state). Triage recommends B bounded by four specific constraints, with the SECURITY.md amendment landing before any code. Yes releases E4 (risk-adjusted 74, the highest unshipped score in its milestone); No cancels or parks it, and triage recommends cancel rather than park if you rule A, because parking is what produced this audit.

artifacts.summary: The largest correction this stage makes is that option B is not a read at all. The issue frames every option as a bounded read; git status --porcelain is process execution inside the user repository, and two consequences were measured in a purpose-built probe rather than reasoned about. It WRITES: plain git status --porcelain advanced .git/index mtime on a clean repo, against a product whose whole posture is read-only, and --no-optional-locks did not. It EXECUTES CODE FROM THE REPOSITORY: with repo-local core.fsmonitor set to a script, git status ran that script twice in one invocation — arbitrary execution under Cargento own identity, sourced from inside the directory being inspected, disarmed by -c core.fsmonitor= . Neither hazard appears in DEC-3, in E4, or in E5. Nine claims were re-derived at v0.17.1; nothing failed to reproduce and three were corrected, including that SECURITY.md:36-37, cited by both E4 and the milestone, is now :62-65. The pathname question resolves against the issue own framing: the product already publishes path fragments today, so "no filenames leave the machine" is a promise it does not make, and the correct wording is SECURITY.md own matching-hints-never-echoed. The audience is unauthenticated 127.0.0.1, where loopback is explicitly not a per-user boundary. The issue self-critique survives and is partly strengthened: DEC-1 amended the network invariant rather than the read one, so the real read-axis precedent is the Spacedock carve-out that landed undecided in PR #10 — making this the second read amendment and the first ever decided — and DEC-1 safety came from shipping an ungated slice first, which B has no counterpart for. Recommendation is B under four bounds, each answering a measured hazard: the two git flags or no probe; a published surface of exactly dirty plus count; one-shot at session end rather than a poll, which also removes index.lock contention; and an off switch matching --no-spacedock. Two traps are flagged for implementation: closing DEC-3 drops the blockedBy edge on all three dependents, but E5 must be re-gated on the unfiled network decision and C7 cancelled rather than released — releasing them is the precise failure this decision was filed to correct.
